Machias and the Submarine Chasers

USS Machias (PG-5) was a 1,177-ton gunboat that had been built for the USN in 1891-92. She was decommissioned on 3 October 1919 and sold to Mexico on 29 October 1920. Renamed Agua Prieta (R 35), she was ultimately scrapped in 1935.

On 9 August 1919 A.J. Alsdorf Corporation of Chicago wrote to the US Navy saying that Mexico was wanting to buy ten second-hand motor launches to use as lighthouse tenders, and they enquired if the US Government would be interested in selling some of the old submarine chasers of the smaller type for supply to Mexico. On 27 August the State Department advised that they saw no objection to permitting the Mexican Government to obtain these launches.

On 3 August 1920, Commodore José de la Llave of the Mexican Navy departed for San Francisco to carry on negotiations for the purchase of several submarine chasers for service on the Pacific coast.

On 26 March 1921 Commodore Miranda of the Mexican Navy who had been charged with inspecting the ex-USS Machias and two ex-US submarine chasers (SC-292 plus one other) visited the US Consulate in Guaymas to obtain information as to where ex-Machias was built and the armament that she carried when forming part of the USN.

On 14 April 1921, Francisco Seldner wrote to Plutarco Calles (who had been the Mexican Secretary of War and Marine from 1 June to 30 November 1920), noting that Calles had ordered the purchase of the gunboat Agua Prieta and the submarine chasers Mayo and Yaqui during his time as Secretary, and that Seldner had inspected and recommended these vessels through Commodore José de la Llave. Seldner also noted that the purchase price for the submarine chasers was $15,000.

Navypedia lists the submarine chasers 18 de Mayo and Yaqui as being ex-USN 110’ submarine chasers built in WW1, and transferred to Mexico. It identifies one of the boats as ex-SC38. Although Navypedia specifies that these boats were transferred to Mexico in 1934, it is most likely that they are in fact the two boats acquired in 1920.

The original USN identity of the two submarine chasers is uncertain. SC38 was an 110’ submarine chaser commissioned on 1 February 1918, which was mined in European waters on 4 September 1919. She was salvaged and sold on 19 December 1919 to Thomas Lee of Ipswich, England. While not impossible, it seems unlikely that SC-38 would have returned to San Francisco in 1920-21 to be sold. SC-292 was another 110’ submarine chaser commissioned on 27 March 1918, which was sold to Barbare Brothers of Tacoma, WA on 3 May 1921 - nineteen days after Seldner’s letter reporting that the boats had been purchased.

Anecdotally, it is possible that the two boats may have been the 110’ submarine chasers SC-289 and SC-297. These two boats were both sold to the same purchaser (E.S. Hough) in San Francisco - SC-297 on 24 September 1920 for 9,000, and SC-289 on 13 January 1921 for $10,800. This fits the known timeline, however no evidence has yet been found that positively links either of these two chasers to Mexico.
